format: 3D models drawn as SVG every frame, with flat SVG decal sheets
status: temporary production asset: procedural 3D models and hand-drawn decals built from the supplied references, pending an illustrator-made model sheet or Rive file

references.drone: IMG_2442.gif (UPLIFT quadcopter, 13 frames) and ScreenRecording_10-24-2026_17-35-25_1.mov (motion art direction)

modelParts.body: generalised cylinder: a spherical bulb rising into the curled flame tip; silhouette solved per pose
modelParts.armL: tapered capsule from a shoulder anchor; abduct/flex/reach
modelParts.armR: tapered capsule from a shoulder anchor; waves
modelParts.legL: tapered capsule from a hip anchor; swings
modelParts.legR: tapered capsule from a hip anchor; swings

decalParts.iris: pupil group moved only by the gaze loop (7 units of travel)
decalParts.mouth: mouth shapes: smile, grin, o, yawn, chew, wobble, snore
decalParts.blush: one cheek, used on both sides
decalParts.apple: green apple prop: whole, bitten, core

modelParts.hull: ellipsoid, lit by a moving highlight
modelParts.arms: four tapered capsules to the motor pods
modelParts.guards: four open rings, split into the halves behind and in front of each rotor
modelParts.rotors: two blades and a blur disc per rotor, spinning in the rotor plane, alternating direction

capabilities: heading (yaw) into the direction of travel
home hover with a slow look round

runtime: No libraries: a small 3D kit (src/pocket/actors/space.js) projects the models with perspective; one requestAnimationFrame loop per actor rewrites the SVG attributes; Web Animations only for travel across the floor and decal details (eyelid, Zs, the tossed apple).
illustratorRequests: A model sheet for the mascot: front, three-quarter, side, back and top views with the flame curl's exact profile, so the procedural body can be matched precisely (or a 3D/Rive source).
The small spur on the upper-left of the flame and the notch under the tip, which the procedural body does not reproduce yet.
Mouth shapes for the full set drawn to the reference style (tongue, teeth, lip line), plus a three-quarter mouth for turned views.
Hands in three states (open palm for waving, fist, holding) and a proper apple-in-hand drawing.
Eye artwork for three-quarter and profile views (currently the front eye is foreshortened on the surface).
Drone: the UPLIFT hull's exact proportions from more angles, the rotor blade shape and a vector brush for the hand-drawn heart trail.
Ideally a Rive file per actor whose state machine exposes yaw/pitch/roll, gaze x/y, expression and the clips listed above.
